{
  "participants": [
    {
      "login": "l0rinc",
      "stance": "objection",
      "note": "requested changes over commit structure, unintended -loglevel behavior changes, kernel logging semantics, and missing test coverage"
    }
  ],
  "claims": [
    {
      "id": "rc:3272563675",
      "kind": "maintenance",
      "harm": "a monolithic commit combining unrelated changes makes meaningful review difficult",
      "quote": "There's a single commit here with a lot of changes that don't look closely related... though in this current state I can't do that meaningfully.",
      "blocking": true,
      "status": "resolved",
      "author_replies": [
        "rc:3273136459",
        "rc:3312181120"
      ],
      "fix_pushed": true,
      "settled_by_id": "rc:3312181120",
      "settled_by_quote": "latest push removes each method in separate commits."
    },
    {
      "id": "rc:3281289661",
      "kind": "correctness",
      "harm": "setting -loglevel unintentionally enables a log category without -debug being set",
      "quote": "Previously, setting a category level at startup stored the override, but it had no visible effect unless the category was also enabled with -debug. Here, setting `-loglevel=net:trace` appears to enable net by itself.",
      "blocking": true,
      "status": "resolved",
      "author_replies": [
        "rc:3312272744"
      ],
      "fix_pushed": true,
      "settled_by_id": "rc:3312272744",
      "settled_by_quote": "It's fixed by making `-loglevel` only update the levels of previously enabled categories."
    },
    {
      "id": "rc:3288013785",
      "kind": "approach",
      "harm": "confusing design that forces conditional categories and unconditional logging levels into the same model",
      "quote": "Seems we have two fundamentally different ways of logging that we're forcing together here... I find this design confusing for multiple reasons",
      "blocking": true,
      "status": "resolved",
      "author_replies": [
        "rc:3312391409"
      ],
      "fix_pushed": true,
      "settled_by_id": "rc:3312391409",
      "settled_by_quote": "changed array declaration and added comment to make this clearer"
    },
    {
      "id": "rc:3289031399",
      "kind": "correctness",
      "harm": "lack of test coverage for the runtime-enable behavior where categories default to Debug even if configured at Trace at startup",
      "quote": "Could we add a test that goes through this runtime-enable path after startup configured the category at Trace?",
      "blocking": true,
      "status": "resolved",
      "author_replies": [
        "rc:3312498305"
      ],
      "fix_pushed": true,
      "settled_by_id": "r:4374002528",
      "settled_by_quote": "adding new tests commits before changes to cover more behaviors"
    },
    {
      "id": "rc:3289129041",
      "kind": "interface",
      "harm": "kernel logging API changes behavior by enabling a category when setting its level",
      "quote": "Previously, setting a category level did not enable the category. Now it looks like setting the level also enables it. Should we adjust this to match the old behavior?",
      "blocking": true,
      "status": "resolved",
      "author_replies": [
        "rc:3312551897"
      ],
      "fix_pushed": true,
      "settled_by_id": "rc:3312551897",
      "settled_by_quote": "In this case I think the new behavior is probably better as there is no point to kernel code setting a level for a category that is ignored because the category is enabled."
    }
  ],
  "support": [],
  "notes": "Initial review round: l0rinc requested changes regarding commit structure, unintentional startup behavior changes with -loglevel, kernel logging semantics, and missing test coverage. ryanofsky split the PR into discrete commits, restored the startup -loglevel behavior, added tests covering runtime and kernel edge cases, and provided rationale for intentional kernel changes."
}

participants.note: requested changes over commit structure, unintended -loglevel behavior changes, kernel logging semantics, and missing test coverage

claims.harm: a monolithic commit combining unrelated changes makes meaningful review difficult
claims.quote: There's a single commit here with a lot of changes that don't look closely related... though in this current state I can't do that meaningfully.
claims.settled_by_quote: latest push removes each method in separate commits.

claims.harm: setting -loglevel unintentionally enables a log category without -debug being set
claims.quote: Previously, setting a category level at startup stored the override, but it had no visible effect unless the category was also enabled with -debug. Here, setting `-loglevel=net:trace` appears to enable net by itself.
claims.settled_by_quote: It's fixed by making `-loglevel` only update the levels of previously enabled categories.

claims.harm: confusing design that forces conditional categories and unconditional logging levels into the same model
claims.quote: Seems we have two fundamentally different ways of logging that we're forcing together here... I find this design confusing for multiple reasons
claims.settled_by_quote: changed array declaration and added comment to make this clearer

claims.harm: lack of test coverage for the runtime-enable behavior where categories default to Debug even if configured at Trace at startup
claims.quote: Could we add a test that goes through this runtime-enable path after startup configured the category at Trace?
claims.settled_by_quote: adding new tests commits before changes to cover more behaviors

claims.harm: kernel logging API changes behavior by enabling a category when setting its level
claims.quote: Previously, setting a category level did not enable the category. Now it looks like setting the level also enables it. Should we adjust this to match the old behavior?
claims.settled_by_quote: In this case I think the new behavior is probably better as there is no point to kernel code setting a level for a category that is ignored because the category is enabled.

result.notes: Initial review round: l0rinc requested changes regarding commit structure, unintentional startup behavior changes with -loglevel, kernel logging semantics, and missing test coverage. ryanofsky split the PR into discrete commits, restored the startup -loglevel behavior, added tests covering runtime and kernel edge cases, and provided rationale for intentional kernel changes.
